newsitem.title: INDIA: Toyota inventory system has defect-Toyoda.
newsitem.headline: Toyota inventory system has defect-Toyoda.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp chairman Shoichiro Toyoda said on Friday that his car company's inventory system needed improvement after a crippling shutdown caused by a fire at a brake parts supplier.

Toyoda, leading a Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) mission to India, told a news conference that the "kanban" inventory system, known as just-in-time, needs to be adjusted to take into account possible interruption of supplies.
The Toyota chairman said his company needs to make sure orders are given to more than one supplier to prevent a crippling cutoff of parts.
Last Saturday a fire at Aisin Seiki Co Ltd's Kariya plant in Aichi Prefecture stopped the delivery of all brake parts supplied to Toyota.
By Tuesday, Japan's largest car maker had shut all of its domestic plants. Normal production is not expected until Monday, a Toyota spokesman in Tokyo told Reuters.

"I still believe this just-in-time production method is a very good method. However, now that we have witnessed this defect, I believe there is a need for taking counter-measures so that this defect would not become larger," Toyoda said.
"Even after this incident our basic philosophy regarding this just-in-time method remains the same, nor is there a need to change it. But we would like to improve this system," he said.
The just-in-time system, introduced in Japan in 1963, is now standard practice for all kinds of manufacturers around the world.
It allows companies to reduce costs by keeping a bare minimum of supplies on hand and instead receive frequent deliveries from suppliers.
"There is a principle in just-in-time to give orders to more than one supplier. I believe there is a need to strictly adhere to this principle," Toyoda said.
An Economic Planning Agency official in Tokyo said that a one-day halt in Toyota's output reduces Japan's overall industrial production by about 0.1 percentage point.
